title: Power Automate Process Mining: analyse processes with object-centric process mining
notes: claim 64: severity major on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: the briefing treats published platform capacity and Fabric billing rules as unanswered questions. Its capacity allocation path omits the Add-ons section, and the current API reference explicitly lists ProcessMiningDataStorage, contrary to the control's applicability warning.

claims.claim: OCPM in Power Automate Process Mining follows multiple objects and object types rather than assigning every event to a single case ID.
claims.quote: Object-centric process mining (OCPM) analyzes processes by following the real objects that interact—such as orders, deliveries, invoices, and payments—rather than forcing every event into a single case ID.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Environment security and Dataverse security roles govern access to process mining.
claims.quote: The process mining capability relies on environment security and Microsoft Dataverse security roles and privileges to grant access to its features in Power Automate.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Environment maker can create, share and contribute to process mining processes.
claims.quote: The Environment maker role can use the process mining capabilities to create, share, and contribute to processes.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Process Mining User can only view created process reports.
claims.quote: The Process Mining User security role can only view created process reports.

claims.claim: Microsoft says not to assign the internal Process Mining Application role to users.
claims.quote: The Process Mining Application is an internal security role that process mining uses. (Process mining was formerly named process advisor). Don't assign this security role to users.

claims.claim: Microsoft says not to modify privileges in Process Mining User or Process Mining Application.
claims.quote: Don't modify the set of privileges in the Process Mining User or Process Mining Application security roles.

claims.claim: OneLake ingestion requires Users can access data stored in OneLake with apps external to Fabric to be switched on.
claims.quote: Ensure that Users can access data stored in OneLake with apps external to the Fabric option is switched on in the OneLake tenant settings.

claims.claim: OneLake ingestion needs a Fabric workspace other than My workspace.
claims.quote: A Fabric workspace that's different from the default My workspace.

claims.claim: The user performing initial Fabric workspace setup for the environment needs Admin.
claims.quote: The Admin role must be attributed to the user performing the initial workspace setup for the environment for the other users in the same environment.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The Fabric workspace must be shared with the Process Insight Prod service principal as Admin.
claims.quote: The Fabric workspace needs to be shared to the Process Insight Prod service principal with an Admin role.

claims.claim: Data must be in final event log format before OneLake ingestion.
claims.quote: All data must be in final event log format and meet the requirements listed in Data requirements. Data should be ready to be mapped to the process mining schema.

claims.claim: No data transformation is available after OneLake ingestion.
claims.quote: No data transformation is available post ingestion.

claims.claim: Stored process data consumes Dataverse storage, mostly file capacity.
claims.quote: Depending on the size of the process data you import, you might run out of Dataverse storage capacity. ... The process data we store uses mostly file capacity.

claims.claim: No autonomous actions are described for OCPM.
claims.quote: Searched: "object-centric" "autonomous" "existing processes". Opened object-centric-overview, object-centric-ingest-event-log, object-centric-process-overview and object-centric-semantic-model; no autonomous business actions were described.

claims.claim: No write actions are described for OCPM.
claims.quote: When you publish a process to Fabric workspace, it creates a new DirectLake semantic model and an empty Power BI report connected to the semantic model.
claims.fix: Replace 'No autonomous or write actions are described for OCPM' with 'No autonomous business actions are described for OCPM; optional export creates a semantic model and report in Fabric.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/object-centric-semantic-model.

claims.claim: Refresh Data in the analytics overview triggers full ingestion and process model creation.
claims.quote: Refresh Data: Button to reload and refresh the displayed analytics with the most recent data (this action triggers the full ingestion and creation of the process model).

claims.claim: The OCPM pages do not name a separate OCPM licence or meter.
claims.quote: Searched: "object-centric" "licensing" "capacity"; "object-centric" "Fabric" "cost". Opened object-centric-overview, object-centric-ingest-event-log, object-centric-process-overview, object-centric-semantic-model and process-advisor-overview; no separate OCPM licence or meter stated.

claims.claim: Whether OCPM data draws on the existing process mining capacity pool is not yet published.
claims.quote: Each Power Automate Premium license adds 50 MB of process mining capacity to a tenant-wide capacity pool up to a total of 100 GB.
claims.fix: Replace the capacity-pool uncertainty with 'OCPM is part of Power Automate Process Mining and is subject to its published process mining capacity pool.' Remove the matching capacity-pool question from Open questions; retain only the narrower question about a separate OCPM-specific meter.

claims.claim: What the optional Fabric export costs on the Fabric side is not yet published.
claims.quote: OneLake storage is billed at a pay-as-you-go rate per GB of data used and doesn't consume Fabric Capacity Units (CUs). Fabric items like lakehouses and warehouses consume OneLake storage.
claims.fix: Replace the Fabric-cost uncertainty with 'Fabric export creates a semantic model on Fabric Lakehouse delta tables. OneLake lakehouse storage is billed pay-as-you-go per GB, and OneLake read and write requests consume Fabric Capacity Units.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/object-centric-semantic-model and https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/onelake/onelake-consumption.

claims.claim: The cited tutorial documents PATCH https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/environments/{environmentId}/allocations?api-version=2022-03-01-preview for allocating add-ons.

Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/rest/api/power-platform/licensing/currency-allocation/patch-currency-allocation-by-environment. The pre-check's missing-endpoint warning is not confirmed.
